prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1119; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a hit while turning left at an intersection. The insured reports that their vehicle was struck by another car while they were completing a left turn, and the policy shows the driver is named on the policy.

Entry 2: Police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Photos taken at the scene confirm some details of the impact, though no independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 3: Vehicle inspection completed. The damage is mostly in line with the described impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage happened before coverage started.

Entry 4: Claimant contacted our office through legal representation and reports a wrist fracture from the collision. The claimant has told the same account in every conversation so far.

Entry 5: Medical records received showing a wrist fracture with treatment that followed a usual course. No earlier injury to the same body area is known at this time.

Entry 6: Treatment has tapered off as the patient has improved. It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash, and the medical review is still open.

Entry 7: Requested prior medical history from the claimant's counsel and reviewed the response. Nothing in the file so far points to a prior injury to the same area.

Entry 8: Liability discussion with the other party's carrier is ongoing. Photos and the police report are being reviewed alongside the vehicle damage estimate.

Entry 9: File remains open pending the medical causation review and a decision on the bodily injury claim. Next follow-up set with claimant's counsel to confirm treatment status.
